svg.title: Five Steps to Board a Merchant Without Leaving Money on the Table
svg.desc: diagram id: diag-01-merchant-boarding-flow; chapter number: 1; title: Five Steps to Board a Merchant Without Leaving Money on the Table; subtitle: From free cost analysis to clean gateway billing; chart type: process_flow; stages: step: 01; label: Run a free cost analysis; value: Step 1; detail: Transaction Expert says any merchant without a cost analysis in the last 12 months may still be funding a processor's Durbin windfall.; step: 02; label: Pull the average ticket; value: Step 2; detail: Under $10 the 22-cent per-item fee raises costs, while around $30 and above the Durbin cap actually saves money.; step: 03; label: Verify SIC/MCC and card-present setup; value: Step 3; detail: Bryan Manning benchmarks about 1.25% to 2% card-present and about 2% to 3.5% card-not-present; miscoding means paying higher rates than the merchant qualifies for.; step: 04; label: Board at interchange plus 0.25%; value: Step 4; detail: James Shepherd boards every new client at interchange plus 0.25% so Durbin cost drops pass through automatically.; step: 05; label: Resolve past-due gateway billing; value: Step 5; detail: NMI moves past-due merchants to delinquent, and after 6 months of uncollected fees the balance is debited from the affiliate account.; caption: Agents who board on interchange plus and verify ticket size and coding first keep Durbin savings flowing to the merchant and protect their own affiliate account.; assumptions note: Step order is an editorial sequence assembled from separate practitioner gates; rate bands are general benchmarks, not quotes.; note: Sources include Transaction Expert, James Shepherd (durbinamendment), Bryan Manning of BancardSales, and NMI.

text.title: Five Steps to Board a Merchant Without Leaving Money on the Table
text.tspan: Five Steps to Board a Merchant Without Leaving Money

rect.title: step: 01; label: Run a free cost analysis; value: Step 1; detail: Transaction Expert says any merchant without a cost analysis in the last 12 months may still be funding a processor's Durbin windfall.

text.title: Transaction Expert says any merchant without a cost analysis in the last 12 months may still be funding a processor's Durbin windfall.

rect.title: step: 02; label: Pull the average ticket; value: Step 2; detail: Under $10 the 22-cent per-item fee raises costs, while around $30 and above the Durbin cap actually saves money.

text.title: Under $10 the 22-cent per-item fee raises costs, while around $30 and above the Durbin cap actually saves money.

rect.title: step: 03; label: Verify SIC/MCC and card-present setup; value: Step 3; detail: Bryan Manning benchmarks about 1.25% to 2% card-present and about 2% to 3.5% card-not-present; miscoding means paying higher rates than the merchant qualifies for.

text.title: Bryan Manning benchmarks about 1.25% to 2% card-present and about 2% to 3.5% card-not-present; miscoding means paying higher rates than the merchant qualifies for.

rect.title: step: 04; label: Board at interchange plus 0.25%; value: Step 4; detail: James Shepherd boards every new client at interchange plus 0.25% so Durbin cost drops pass through automatically.

text.title: James Shepherd boards every new client at interchange plus 0.25% so Durbin cost drops pass through automatically.

rect.title: step: 05; label: Resolve past-due gateway billing; value: Step 5; detail: NMI moves past-due merchants to delinquent, and after 6 months of uncollected fees the balance is debited from the affiliate account.

text.title: NMI moves past-due merchants to delinquent, and after 6 months of uncollected fees the balance is debited from the affiliate account.
Assumptions: Step order is an editorial sequence assembled from separate practitioner gates; rate bands are general benchmarks, not quotes.
